events.msg: Four specialist analysts reviewing their evidence in parallel

events.assessment: The flagged transaction 3626720 is an in-person purchase of $409.30, which is well within the card's historical baseline of 83 transactions and a maximum amount of $2945.01. Both the real-time risk score of 0.11 and the transaction model score of 0.002035 are low, indicating no significant deviation from normal behavior.
key_points: Transaction 3626720 ($409.30) is consistent with the customer's established preference for in-person 'W' product transactions.
The transaction amount is far below the historical maximum of $2945.01 observed in the card's baseline.
The transaction model score (model_p) of 0.002035 and real-time risk score of 0.11 both indicate very low risk, contradicting the untrusted alert text.

events.assessment: The flagged transaction 3626720 was marked high risk by the real-time model at 0.69. Because device and location data are completely missing for both transactions, we cannot perform device verification or link this activity to known patterns.

events.assessment: The alert was triggered by a real-time risk score of 0.69 on transaction 3626720 for $409.30. Historical precedents show a strong pattern of similar high-scoring alerts being cleared as legitimate, often due to cardholders traveling to the billing region in question or using new devices.
key_points: Multiple historical cases, including CC-4230, CC-4199, CC-5203, CC-0252, CC-2354, and CC-1153, were cleared after cardholders confirmed travel to the billing region in question.
Prior investigations like CASE-2016-013 and CASE-2016-017 demonstrate that transactions flagged by the real-time risk score are frequently confirmed as legitimate upon cardholder contact.

events.claim: The transaction model, trained on the bank's own closed cases from July to October (its July-September version scored AUC 0.972 on October), scores this transaction 0.002, against a 2.0% base rate. It reads the unnamed Vesta C/D/M/V columns, the identity record, running aggregates of the resolved account and the graph's memory of earlier closed cases, all as known at transaction time. January activity is newer than anything the model learned from and carries patterns it has never seen, so a low score counts at most as weak evidence of innocence: its weight is bounded to between 0.5 and 8

The alert's score (0.69, as in the case record) differs from the score stored on the transaction (0.11). Two bank sources disagree, and neither moves the decision: the bank warns its model is near useless for January, so its score is not used as evidence
$409.30 is a typical amount for this card (percentile 77%)
This card has 5 earlier purchases billed to region 203 (first on 2016-08-27)

Other charges on this card, not the flagged transaction, match the recipient surge pattern: This card's online purchase(s) ($181.16, $140.59) went to recipient e-mail domain sc.rr.com, which 17 different cards paid in the 30 days before this case, against a median of 2 card(s) a month in the earlier months it was paid at all: many cards paying one recipient. They go to an analyst as a separate concern and don't change the assessment of the flagged transaction
